codes.description: High Speed CAN Communication Bus
causes: Open or shorted CAN high/low wiring
Module shorting or loading the bus
Aftermarket device on the data link
codes.notes: With the battery disconnected, resistance across CAN high and CAN low at the DLC (SAE J1962 pins 6 and 14) typically reads about 60 ohms on a two-terminator high-speed CAN bus (general guideline — verify against OEM specification and network topology). Isolate a shorted or loaded bus by disconnecting modules one at a time while watching bus voltages or a lab scope pattern. Check module powers and grounds before condemning a module.

Control Module Communication Bus Off
causes: CAN bus shorted to ground or voltage
CAN high shorted to CAN low
codes.notes: Set by a module that detected so many transmit errors that it removed itself from the bus (bus-off). Later J2012 revisions label this code Bus A. Check bus voltages and termination resistance, then isolate by disconnecting modules one at a time; a lab scope on CAN high and CAN low quickly shows shorts and noise.

Lost Communication With ECM/PCM "A"
symptoms: No scan tool communication with ECM
causes: Loss of ECM power or ground
Blown ECM fuse or failed relay
Open or shorted CAN wiring at ECM
codes.notes: Determine which modules set the code and whether the ECM communicates with the scan tool at all. Voltage-drop test ECM powers, grounds, and ignition feed under load, then check CAN wiring at the ECM connector. Intermittent U0100 often traces to battery terminals, ground straps, or connector problems.

codes.description: Lost Communication With TCM
symptoms: Transmission in failsafe or limp mode
causes: Loss of TCM power or ground
codes.notes: Many TCMs are mounted on or inside the transmission, where fluid wicking or heat can damage connectors. Verify TCM power, ground, and ignition feed and check CAN wiring before replacing the TCM; a replacement TCM usually requires programming per OEM procedure.

codes.description: Lost Communication With Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
symptoms: ABS, traction, and stability lamps on
causes: Loss of ABS module power or ground
CAN wiring fault to ABS module
codes.notes: The ABS module normally has a separate high-current (pump and valve) feed and an ignition feed; check both along with the ground under load. Inspect the module connector for water intrusion. Base brakes normally remain functional, but ABS and stability control are disabled, so road test with caution.

Lost Communication With Steering Angle Sensor Module
causes: Steering angle sensor power or ground loss
CAN wiring fault at steering column
Connector fault at clockspring or sensor
codes.notes: The steering angle sensor is often mounted with the clockspring at the top of the steering column. SRS work requires following OEM disable/enable procedures: disconnect the battery and wait the OEM-specified time before working near the clockspring or driver airbag, and reconnect and verify the system per OEM procedure. A replaced or disconnected sensor usually requires calibration with a scan tool.
